Agent Setu is an independent, unofficial application. It is not developed, endorsed, sponsored or operated by India Post, the Department of Posts, the Ministry of Communications or India Post Payments Bank. It does not connect to any departmental system. Scheme information, rates and commission rules in the app are for personal record-keeping and guidance only; always verify with the latest official orders and your Post Office.

On Vivo, Oppo, Realme and OnePlus: also allow Auto-launch and Background activity.
On Samsung: in Battery, make sure Agent Setu is not in Sleeping apps.

Summary written from public information, September 2026.

Life insurance run by the Department of Posts since 1884.
For government and semi-government employees, some professionals (such as doctors, engineers, lawyers and chartered accountants) and employees of listed companies - check eligibility at your Post Office.
Plans: whole life, endowment, convertible whole life, anticipated endowment (money back), joint life for couples, and a children's policy.
Low premiums, with bonus added as declared each year.
Premium can count for tax deduction under Section 80C (old tax regime).

Life insurance for people living in rural areas, since 1995.
Plans: Gram Suraksha (whole life), Gram Santosh (endowment), Gram Suvidha (convertible), Gram Sumangal (money back), Gram Priya (10-year money back) and a children's policy.
Low premiums suited to rural families, with bonus as declared.
Premium can count for tax deduction under Section 80C (old tax regime).

Fixed deposit for 1, 2, 3 or 5 years.
Minimum ₹1,000, in multiples of ₹100; no upper limit.
Interest is calculated every quarter and paid every year.
The 5-year deposit qualifies for tax deduction under Section 80C (old tax regime).
Can be closed early after 6 months, with lower interest.

Save a fixed amount every month for 5 years.
Minimum ₹100 a month, in multiples of ₹10; no upper limit.
Interest is compounded every quarter and paid with the deposits at maturity.
Loan up to half of the balance after 12 instalments.
Can be closed early after 3 years.

Deposit once and get interest every month for 5 years.
Minimum ₹1,000; maximum ₹9 lakh in a single account and ₹15 lakh in a joint account.
The deposit comes back after 5 years.
Can be closed early after 1 year, with a deduction.

5-year savings certificate.
Minimum ₹1,000, in multiples of ₹100; no upper limit.
Interest is compounded every year and paid at maturity.
Qualifies for tax deduction under Section 80C (old tax regime).
Can be pledged as security for a loan.

Certificate in which the money doubles over a fixed period, set by the rate when it is bought.
Minimum ₹1,000, in multiples of ₹100; no upper limit.
Can be cashed after 2 years 6 months.
Can be transferred to another person or pledged for a loan.

For people aged 60 or more (and, under conditions, some retired people from 55 and retired defence personnel from 50).
Minimum ₹1,000; maximum ₹30 lakh.
Interest is paid every quarter; the term is 5 years and can be extended by 3 years.
Qualifies for tax deduction under Section 80C (old tax regime).

15-year savings account for long-term goals.
Deposit ₹500 to ₹1.5 lakh in a financial year.
Interest and the maturity amount are tax-free; deposits qualify under Section 80C (old tax regime).
Partial withdrawal from the 7th year; loan from the 3rd year.
Can be extended in blocks of 5 years.

Savings account for a girl child, opened before she turns 10.
Deposit ₹250 to ₹1.5 lakh in a financial year, for 15 years.
Matures 21 years after opening; partial withdrawal for education after she turns 18.
Interest and the maturity amount are tax-free; deposits qualify under Section 80C (old tax regime).
